title: Google says Big Sleep foiled an imminent in-the-wild SQLite exploit
summary: In a 15 July 2025 post by Kent Walker, Google reported that Big Sleep, an AI agent developed by Google DeepMind and Google Project Zero, used intel from Google Threat Intelligence to discover CVE-2025-6965, a critical SQLite flaw that was known only to threat actors and at risk of being exploited, which Google believes is the first time an AI agent has been used to directly foil efforts to exploit a vulnerability in the wild. Google said it will keep reporting Big Sleep findings through its industry-standard disclosure process, lists publicly disclosed Big Sleep vulnerabilities on its issue tracker, and linked a white paper on building AI agents that safeguard privacy, mitigate the risks of rogue actions, and operate with human oversight and transparency.
